title: DXF DICTIONARY entry-kind preservation and FIELD route
mode: Primary-source web research plus local source audit; plan-only
scope: Separate DICTIONARY flag 280, entry handle codes 350/360, owner topology, and FIELD internal references.
Compare current Autodesk references with ezdxf and ACadRust source/release behavior.
Refine the existing PAR-20/7G implementation sequence around preserving per-entry source edge codes without adding fixtures or test lanes.

sources.name: Autodesk current DICTIONARY DXF reference
observations: Documents group 280 as dictionary hard-owner flag, 281 as duplicate-cloning policy, and group 350 as the entry object handle.
Does not state that flag 280 determines the code of every dictionary entry.

sources.name: Autodesk general DXF group-code ranges
observations: Classifies 350-359 as soft-owner IDs and 360-369 as hard-owner IDs.

sources.name: Autodesk AutoCAD 2012 DXF reference
observations: Its DICTIONARY group-code table likewise lists flag 280 separately from entry group 350.
Separates flag 281 cloning semantics from flag 280 hard-owner semantics.

sources.name: Autodesk FIELD DXF reference and developer description
observations: FIELD child handles use group 360 and expression object IDs use group 331.
NOD ACAD_FIELDLIST to FIELDLIST is distinct from an entity extension dictionary's ACAD_FIELD to FIELD route.

sources.name: ACadRust v0.6.5 release and writer source
sources.revision: GitHub release v0.6.5 dated 2026-10-18; current source package version 0.6.5; earlier v0.5.5 note accessed for history
observations: v0.6.5/current writer combines dictionary-wide hard-owner state with per-entry/canonical hard-owner state.
Its current source comment names ACAD_FIELD, ACAD_LAYOUT, and ACAD_PLOTSTYLENAME as canonical hard-owner keys and claims cross-application agreement.
The earlier v0.5.5 release note explicitly describes ACAD_FIELD and a BricsCAD comparison; this narrower earlier note does not independently verify all three current canonical keys.
limits: No ACadRust executable or native CAD consumer was run; source comments are not independent interoperability evidence.
The broader current-source claim conflicts with the generic Autodesk DICTIONARY table and earlier BricsCAD audit evidence, so no universal key rule is adopted.

sources.name: ezdxf current DICTIONARY implementation and docs
observations: The parser accepts both group 350 and 360 entry handles.
The implementation stores one dictionary-level value code, updated as each entry is loaded, then exports all dictionary entries with that one code.
A mixed-code dictionary therefore cannot be validated by ezdxf rewrite fidelity; output can depend on the final encountered edge.
limits: Mutable master source was not pinned to a full commit in this pass and is not used as a normative oracle.

sources.name: LibreDWG release history and current writer source
observations: NEWS contains a historical DICTIONARY hard_owner 350/360 writer fix.
The current writer contains generated/macro-based object output, but current key-by-key behavior was not executed or independently recovered in this research pass.
limits: Historical release notes do not establish present output behavior or an expected-value rule.

sources.name: Local libdxfrw parser/writer/test source
observations: The parser accepts group 350 and 360 but Entry stores only name and handle.
Ordinary dictionary writers choose 360 when hardOwner is 1 and 350 otherwise; the generated NOD uses a separate group-350 path.
The current typed model cannot preserve mixed per-entry edge kinds across parse/write.
limits: The source audit did not run a generated parse/write control; reproduce output loss in the owning fast test before making production code changes.
dx_iface intentionally refuses FIELD/FIELDLIST serialization; a low-level writer test must not imply adapter support.

existingSubplansRefined: PAR-20/7G: preserve each parsed DICTIONARY entry's 350/360 edge kind independently of group 280.
PAR-20/7G: keep construction defaults, the regenerated NOD route, and the ACAD_FIELD extension-dictionary candidate as separate policies.
PAR-20/7G: use literal ASCII/Binary output scans for edge code and typed readback only for structural graph closure.

limitations: Autodesk's documented generic DICTIONARY table does not exclude producer-specific 360 entries.
ACadRust v0.6.5's broader canonical-key claims were not validated against raw AutoCAD, ODA, or LibreDWG output in this pass.
ezdxf's mutable source accepts 350/360 but stores one value code per dictionary; it is not a per-entry preservation oracle.
No generated local reproduction, peer runtime, native application, external sample, or full suite was used.
